The search turned up one main answer: local observability in `wrangler dev` is on by default in recent releases, and you can turn it off with an environment variable.

- **Default-on, with opt-out:** wrangler dev and the Vite plugin now capture request traces and console logs into the Local Explorer's Observability tab out of the box — previously this was opt-in behind X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=true. Set X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=false to opt out. The same change is listed in the wrangler 4.118.0 release notes, dated July 31, 2026 (Enable local observability capture by default in dev).
- **Conflicting earlier info:** A July 23, 2026 release (wrangler 4.114.0) said while this is in testing it's off by default; set X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=true to turn it on. It will be on by default in the public release. The later release notes supersede that.
- **What it captures:** wrangler dev and vite dev automatically capture structured OpenTelemetry traces and correlated console logs during local Worker invocations. You can view them in the Local Explorer's Observability tab.
- **Not the same as the `observability` block in wrangler.jsonc:** The Flavio Copes article covers enabling `observability` in `wrangler.jsonc` to store and search logs in the Cloudflare dashboard for deployed Workers. That is a separate, production-side setting, and the results don't say whether it affects local dev. I didn't find a documented way to disable local capture beyond the environment variable above.

content.text:
Your Worker's `console.log` output still prints in the `wrangler dev` terminal. Starting with wrangler 4.118.0 (released July 31, 2026), `wrangler dev` and the Cloudflare Vite plugin also capture OpenTelemetry request traces and the console logs tied to them. You can view these in the **Observability tab of the Local Explorer**. To stop that capture, set `X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY=false` before you start the dev server, for example `$env:X_LOCAL_OBSERVABILITY = "false"; npx wrangler dev` in PowerShell. Before 4.118.0 this was off unless you set the variable to `true`. The `observability` block in `wrangler.jsonc` is a different setting: it sends logs from deployed Workers to the Cloudflare dashboard. The release notes don't say whether it affects local dev.

Sources:
- [wrangler 4.118.0: local observability on by default](https://releases.sh/release/rel_8_P1FMWi7cB_iDXTx-lAU-wrangler-4-118-0-enables-local-observability-by-default-fixes-dev-shutdown-leaks)
- [Local dev observability: traces, logs, SQL query endpoint](https://releases.sh/release/rel_sLBHvKoHq2yYEz_ebczQ4-local-dev-observability-traces-logs-sql-query-endpoint)
- [Workers Vite plugin v1.50.0: local observability by default](https://releases.sh/release/rel_i_IjQR4VkcS74NNt2j8VY-workers-vite-plugin-v1-50-0-enables-local-observability-capture-by-default-in)
- [Cloudflare blog: debug Workers with local tracing](https://blog.cloudflare.com/tag/workers-observability/)
